incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR, chapter S-31.1, including sections 2 to 5, 17, 18, 19, 21, 22, 30, 31, 32, 42, and 43, as applicable to constitution, articles, directors, registered office, and share capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec, administered by the Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for constitution of a legal person under the Business Corporations Act, including the articles of constitution and required notice of registered office and directors, followed by registration in the Registre des entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. Shares may be issued for consideration authorized by the board, subject to the articles and the Business Corporations Act. Quebec incorporation does not require a statutory escrow account. The corporation should document share subscriptions, consideration received, and the issued share ledger.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation accept the subscription by [Subscriber] for [number and class] shares for aggregate consideration of CAD [amount], payable as stated in the subscription agreement; that the registered office be established at [Quebec address]; and that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to hold office until resignation or replacement. The officers are authorized to open bank and payment accounts, execute incorporation and tax registrations, and take all actions necessary to commence the Corporation’s email infrastructure and newsletter hosting business. The corporate records, securities register, and resolutions shall be maintained at the registered office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Select corporate name and verify Quebec availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online services and enterprise-name search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a distinctive French-compliant or bilingual corporate name, conduct an enterprise-register search, and obtain a Nuans report if a federal corporation will instead be used. Avoid names that are confusingly similar, misleading, or inconsistent with Quebec language requirements. Reserve or submit the selected name through the applicable online incorporation workflow.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an amended name, provide supporting distinctiveness information, or incorporate under a numbered corporation and file a permitted assumed name later.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online constitution service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of constitution, registered-office address, director information, share classes, transfer restrictions, and restrictions on corporate activities if desired. Confirm that at least one director is appointed and that the articles accurately reflect the intended ownership and governance structure. Execute documents using the accepted electronic signature process; notarization is generally not required for standard online constitution filings unless a specific supporting document requires it.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership and control information where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected fields or upload deficiencies through the registry portal. If the registry issues a formal notice, respond within the stated deadline and resubmit the corrected instrument with an explanatory letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File constitution and pay registry fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the constitution application and all required schedules electronically, pay the applicable filing fee in Canadian dollars, and retain the payment receipt and submission number. The stated USD amount is an indicative conversion of the official Quebec-dollar fee and must be verified at filing because fees and exchange rates change. Use certified translations only where supporting documents are not accepted in French or English.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the portal for queries, correct the filing promptly, and preserve the original submission evidence. If a decision is adverse, request administrative reconsideration or use the statutory review or appeal mechanism identified in the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain constitution evidence and complete registry registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and Registre des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the certificate or confirmation of constitution, Quebec enterprise number, current enterprise register extract, and filed articles. Verify the legal name, directors, registered office, activity description, and registration status. Correct any inaccurate information through the prescribed amendment filing without delay.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File an amendment or correction with the Registraire des entreprises. For a rejected amendment, cure the stated deficiency and request reprocessing; retain a current certified extract for banking and contracting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt organizational governance and issue shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation’s registered office and corporate records repository
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first directors’ meeting or execute unanimous written resolutions. Adopt the registered office, appoint officers, approve banking and payment accounts, approve the business plan, authorize tax registrations, approve shareholder subscriptions, receive consideration, issue shares, and update the securities register and minute book. Obtain director consents and conflict disclosures. Notarization is not normally required, but preserve signed originals and electronic audit trails.
required_dossiers: Share certificate or electronic issuance record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an issuance or resolution is defective, obtain ratification by the board or shareholders where legally available, correct the securities register, and obtain legal advice before making further issuances.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete federal and Quebec tax registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online and Revenu Québec online services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a CRA business number and register for applicable GST/HST, payroll, and corporate income-tax accounts. Register for Quebec sales tax and other applicable Quebec tax accounts with Revenu Québec. Determine filing obligations based on taxable supplies, payroll, nexus, and permanent-establishment facts. Maintain separate accounting records for federal and Quebec filings.
required_dossiers: Projected taxable revenues and payroll data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected registration data through the relevant portal or telephone service, submit missing authorization documents, and document the effective date of each account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Implement operating compliance for email infrastructure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, Commission d’accès à l’information du Québec, and Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission, as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commercial launch, implement privacy governance under Quebec privacy legislation and applicable federal privacy law, consent and unsubscribe controls under Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation, breach-response procedures, data-retention controls, vendor agreements, and cybersecurity safeguards. Review whether any personal information is transferred outside Quebec or Canada and document required assessments, contractual controls, and customer disclosures.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address regulator inquiries through a documented remediation plan, preserve relevant records, notify affected parties where legally required, and obtain specialized privacy counsel for material incidents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a standard software, email API, and newsletter hosting platform without manufacturing, regulated telecommunications facilities, or physical environmental discharges. Municipal authorities remain competent for zoning, occupancy, construction, and local fire requirements.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general Quebec manufacturing or industrial operating permit is ordinarily required for the stated SaaS activity. Separate permits may apply if the corporation operates data-centre equipment, constructs premises, installs generators, stores fuel, or performs regulated telecommunications activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l’Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for ordinary office-based SaaS operations with no prescribed project, industrial process, significant land disturbance, or regulated discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine industrial wastewater, process VOC, or manufacturing waste is expected. Municipal sewer, hazardous-material, refrigerant, fuel, electronic-waste, and waste-diversion rules apply where relevant. Any data-centre cooling discharge, backup-generator emissions, fuel storage, construction activity, or hazardous-waste handling must be separately assessed under Quebec environmental legislation and applicable municipal bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No sector-specific industrial clearance is ordinarily required for an office-based SaaS business. The premises must comply with municipal occupancy and zoning rules, Quebec building and fire-safety requirements, and applicable workplace health and safety obligations administered by the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail. Fire alarms, emergency exits, electrical systems, structural loads, and generator or server-room installations require inspection or permits where mandated by the building owner, municipality, or applicable code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and My Business Account, administers federal corporate income tax and GST/HST. Revenu Québec administers Québec corporate income tax and Québec sales tax (QST), including registration through its online services. The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers import and export customs processes through the CARM commercial accounting platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act or provincially under the Québec Business Corporations Act, as applicable. 2. Obtain or confirm a nine-digit federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA through Business Registration Online, by telephone, or through the incorporation process where integrated registration is available. 3. Register the corporation for a CRA corporation income tax program account, generally identified by the RC program identifier, if required for filing and administration. 4. Register for a GST/HST program account, identified by the RT program identifier, before making taxable supplies where the corporation is required to register; voluntary registration is generally available if the corporation is engaged in commercial activity. 5. Register with Revenu Québec for Québec corporate income tax where the corporation is resident in Québec or otherwise carries on business in Québec and is subject to Québec income tax filing obligations. 6. Register for QST using the Revenu Québec registration process where the corporation is required to collect QST or elects voluntary registration. A small supplier generally becomes required to register for GST/HST and QST when taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters, subject to applicable rules and exclusions. 7. Register for payroll, import-export, information-return, and other program accounts only when the relevant activities arise. 8. A non-resident corporation must determine whether it is carrying on business in Canada, has a permanent establishment, makes taxable supplies in Canada, or is required to register under the non-resident digital economy rules. A non-resident corporation may need a BN, corporate income tax account, GST/HST account, QST account, or several accounts depending on its activities. 9. Maintain legal-name, registered-office, director, beneficial-ownership, banking, and authorized-representative information consistently across federal, Québec, CRA, Revenu Québec, payment processor, and customs records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Canadian business corporation is generally taxed as a separate legal entity and does not have a United States-style check-the-box election or general pass-through election. A corporation may qualify for the federal small business deduction and Québec small business regimes if statutory conditions are met. A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) classification may provide access to preferential corporate rates, refundable taxes, and related regimes, but it is not an elective classification and depends on ownership and control facts. A corporation may make specific elections under the Income Tax Act and Québec tax legislation, including elections concerning capital property, amalgamations, wind-ups, reorganizations, eligible dividends, tax pools, and certain partnership or trust transactions. GST/HST and QST elections may apply to consolidated, closely related, real-property, financial, or simplified non-resident arrangements. Canada does not provide a general entity-classification election that converts an incorporated business into a transparent entity for Canadian income tax purposes. Hybrid-entity treatment may create treaty, foreign tax credit, withholding, or anti-hybrid issues and requires transaction-specific analysis.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Canada uses a federal GST/HST system administered by the CRA and a separate Québec sales tax (QST) system administered by Revenu Québec. Québec generally applies 5% GST and 9.975% QST to taxable supplies, producing a combined headline rate of 14.975% when both taxes apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, excluding specified supplies and subject to the detailed small-supplier rules, in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters generally triggers GST/HST registration. A generally corresponding CAD 30,000 threshold applies for QST registration, with separate rules for specified suppliers of cross-border digital services and property. Registration can be voluntary before the threshold is exceeded where the legal conditions are satisfied. Once registered, the supplier must charge, collect, report, and remit the applicable tax, subject to zero-rating and input tax credit or input tax refund rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Québec do not generally impose a universal real-time electronic invoicing, government clearance, or digital tax-stamping mandate for ordinary B2B or B2C supplies, including ordinary SaaS and email infrastructure services. Invoices and receipts must contain sufficient information to substantiate GST/HST input tax credits and QST input tax refunds, including supplier identity and registration numbers, date, consideration, tax rate, tax amount, and applicable disclosure information. Electronic records are generally acceptable if they remain reliable, accessible, readable, and capable of audit verification. CRA and Revenu Québec may require electronic filing for specified returns, elections, or registrants, but this is not equivalent to invoice clearance. Payment processors such as Stripe do not replace the supplier's invoicing, tax collection, filing, or record-retention obligations. Québec language requirements may apply to commercial documents and customer-facing communications under the Charter of the French Language, subject to applicable exemptions and implementation rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada may generally be zero-rated for GST/HST where the statutory export conditions are satisfied, including export from Canada and prescribed documentary evidence. For a bulk transactional email API, newsletter hosting platform, or other SaaS business, the principal export issue is usually the place of supply of services rather than customs export. Services supplied to a non-resident may be zero-rated for GST/HST where the recipient is not resident in Canada and the statutory conditions are met, including applicable exclusions for services relating to real property, tangible personal property, personal services, or services performed in respect of Canadian activities or property. A non-resident customer using cloud communications services partly or wholly in Canada may prevent or limit zero-rating depending on the precise service and use facts. QST zero-rating may apply to qualifying exported services where the service is supplied to a non-resident and is not acquired for consumption, use, or supply in Québec, subject to statutory exclusions and place-of-supply rules. Services supplied to Canadian or Québec customers generally remain taxable at the applicable GST/HST and QST rates. The supplier should obtain and retain evidence of customer residence, contractual recipient identity, billing address, payment records, user-location data where relevant, service-use facts, and the contractual allocation of service delivery. Zero-rating is not established solely by foreign currency payment, a foreign email address, a foreign bank account, or incorporation of the customer outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For tangible goods exported from Canada: commercial invoice, export declaration where required, applicable CARM or CBSA export records, packing list, transport document or bill of lading, proof of export, and customer or consignee details.

For exports requiring an export declaration, the applicable Canadian export reporting record, including the required export data and transaction reference, retained in accordance with CBSA requirements.
Bill of lading, airway bill, courier record, or equivalent carrier evidence showing movement of goods outside Canada.
Proof of delivery or foreign import documentation where available and relevant.
For foreign-currency receipts: sales contract, invoice, bank statement, payment processor settlement record, and remittance evidence connecting the payment to the exported supply.

For pure digital SaaS, email API, and newsletter hosting services: no customs export declaration or bill of lading is ordinarily required because no tangible goods cross the border. The substantiation file should instead include the master services agreement, order form, invoice, non-resident customer identification, tax-residence evidence, billing and payment records, service logs, and evidence supporting the place and nature of use.

GST/HST and QST registration numbers, tax coding, zero-rated invoice treatment, general-ledger reconciliation, return workpapers, and supporting records for input tax credits or QST input tax refunds.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated to Canada within 180 days. Foreign-exchange conversion and repatriation are therefore not generally conditions for GST/HST or QST zero-rating, although payment and banking evidence remains relevant to audit substantiation. If zero-rating is incorrectly claimed, CRA or Revenu Québec may reassess the uncollected GST/HST or QST, deny input tax credits or QST input tax refunds, and assess applicable arrears interest and penalties. Penalties may include failure-to-file, failure-to-remit, failure-to-register, gross-negligence, repeated-failure, or false-statement penalties depending on the conduct and statutory provision. A registrant that charged tax but failed to remit it may remain liable for the tax despite customer-payment issues. Fraudulent or knowingly false records may expose the corporation and responsible individuals to civil penalties and criminal prosecution, including fines and imprisonment under applicable federal or Québec legislation. CBSA export-reporting breaches may result in administrative monetary penalties, detention or seizure, and enforcement action. Records supporting zero-rating, tax collection, and refunds should generally be retained for at least six years from the end of the relevant tax year, subject to longer retention requirements, pending objections, litigation, or specific statutory rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible currency regime for current account transactions under IMF Article VIII. Capital account transactions are generally permitted with prior regulatory notification or approval from the Bank of Canada or OSFI for investments above CAD 100 million or certain portfolio investments. Profit remittances are permitted subject to 25% Canadian withholding tax on dividends, filing of T1134 forms, and repatriation reporting to FINTRAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Exporters must file a report with the Bank of Canada through the Canadian Importers and Exporters Reporting System if the transaction value exceeds CAD 10,000. Conversion occurs at prevailing market rates with no statutory surrender ratios or timelines.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital EMIs due to licensing requirements under the Payment Services Act and strict AML obligations. Canadian corporations may use licensed fintech payment processors such as Stripe for cross-border settlements but must maintain full KYC/AML compliance and cannot route through unlicensed offshore entities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital KYC and video interview onboarding permitted for standard corporate accounts under the Bank Act and OSFI guidelines. Physical presence and in-person KYC interview required for accounts exceeding CAD 250,000, high-risk sectors, or when beneficial ownership exceeds 25%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate ownership chart, articles of incorporation, shareholder agreements, and declarations confirming beneficial owners above 25% threshold
Bank statements, audited financial statements, tax returns, and independent third-party confirmation of capital injection origin
Enhanced due diligence reports, senior management attestations, and PEP screening results from approved databases

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires via SWIFT MT103 using purpose codes 'EQTY' for equity contributions or 'LOAN' for intercompany loans. All transactions require board resolutions, source of funds evidence, and KYC documentation. Canadian banks perform verification per OSFI Guideline B-9 on foreign currency transactions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements via SWIFT MT103 for international payments or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600. Trade settlements cleared through correspondent banking networks with proper purpose coding and compliance documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canada Business Corporations Act annual return, if federally incorporated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File annually within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary date; file electronically where available.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in compliance notices and administrative dissolution proceedings. Federal filing fee is generally CAD 12, approximately USD 9, subject to exchange-rate and fee changes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec annual updating declaration and annual registration fee, if Quebec-incorporated or registered to do business in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File during the annual updating period prescribed by the Registraire, generally commencing on the corporation's anniversary date and extending through the prescribed following period shown in the enterprise register account.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The annual registration fee becomes delinquent and may accrue prescribed charges. Continued non-compliance may lead to cancellation of registration or administrative dissolution. The fee is indexed; a typical corporation fee is approximately CAD 90, or USD 65.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File within six months after the corporation's taxation year-end. Any balance is generally due two months after year-end, or three months for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties generally apply where tax is owing, with arrears interest accruing daily. Repeated or extended non-filing may trigger demands, reassessments, collection action, and loss of certain tax benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return, where Quebec corporate tax filing is applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File within six months after the corporation's taxation year-end. Corporate tax instalments and balance-due rules apply separately.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and prescribed interest may apply. Continued non-compliance may result in assessments, collection measures, director-liability exposure in applicable cases, and restrictions on tax accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of directors, registered office, corporate status, and beneficial ownership information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada or the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, according to the corporation's incorporation and registration status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirm through the applicable annual return or annual updating declaration and report changes within the statutory change-reporting period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain accurate information may result in filing rejection, compliance notices, penalties, administrative dissolution or cancellation of registration, and potential director or officer liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private corporation is generally not required to obtain an annual independent audit solely because of revenue, assets, or employee count. Under the Canada Business Corporations Act, shareholders may dispense with an auditor by the required unanimous resolution where permitted. Quebec corporate requirements and financing, shareholder, lender, grant, or contractual obligations must be reviewed separately. Publicly accountable entities and entities subject to sector-specific regulation generally require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian private enterprises generally use Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises under Canadian GAAP. IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises and may be adopted by eligible entities. Financial statements must also comply with applicable federal or Quebec corporate-law requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain and review the securities register, beneficial ownership information, and individuals-with-significant-control or ultimate-beneficiary records at least annually. Federal corporations must provide required individuals-with-significant-control information with the annual return and report changes within 15 days. Quebec entities must disclose and update ultimate-beneficiary information through the enterprise register and applicable updating filings. Record each share transfer, issuance, redemption, or ownership-control change promptly; an unchanged annual confirmation does not replace mandatory event-driven updates.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute book containing shareholder and director resolutions and meeting minutes
Articles, certificates, bylaws, shareholder agreements, and filed corporate records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_government_renewal_fees: Approximately USD 9 for a federal CBCA annual return, or approximately USD 65 for a Quebec annual registration fee, depending on incorporation and registration status; tax returns generally have no government filing fee.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300-1,200 annually for registered-office, records-office, and corporate-secretarial support in Quebec; a separate agent-for-service requirement may apply depending on the incorporation jurisdiction.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000-20,000 for a basic private-company audit; complexity, revenue volume, related-party activity, transaction volume, reporting requirements, and group structure may materially increase the fee.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal and Quebec general corporate rate of 26.5% (federal Part I 15% plus Quebec 11.5%). The 15% federal headline reflects the 38% statutory rate reduced by the 10% provincial abatement and 13% general rate reduction. Quebec levies its own 11.5% general rate on taxable income allocated to Quebec.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) earning active business income can access the federal Small Business Deduction (9% federal rate on the first CAD 500,000) and the Quebec small business deduction (3.2% Quebec rate on the first CAD 500,000), producing a combined 12.2% effective rate on that band. The target CA_CORP, if ultimately controlled by a non-resident, is not a CCPC and therefore cannot claim the small business deduction; its effective combined rate is generally 26.5%. Additional incentives include the federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR and ED) investment tax credit (15% non-refundable for large/non-CCPCs, 35% refundable for qualifying CCPCs), the Quebec SR and ED credit (up to 30% of eligible wages), and the Quebec e-business development tax credit for qualifying interactive digital/email platform wages (up to 30% refundable credit subject to eligibility conditions and program dates).
